en.p: There are 16 balls and six empty boxes, labeled with the natural numbers 1 through 6, one number each. Using one die, the following trial is performed.

box: Roll the die once. Let $k$ be the number rolled.
If $k$ is odd, put one ball into each of the boxes labeled 1, 3, and 5;
if $k$ is even, put one ball into each box labeled with a divisor of $k$.

en.p: After repeating this trial 4 times, given that the total number of balls in the six boxes is odd, what is the probability that the box labeled 3 contains exactly one more ball than the box labeled 2? [4 points]
